result:
I finished all 3 tasks of unit 479, but only partly reached its goal. A station about 15 dB over the noise now mostly makes bars; one about 10 dB over still makes none. Both of those synthetic tests are still red and left named in the report. Every task is committed and pushed to `main`, and `output.md` is written at the root but not committed, as in earlier units. No recording was read.

| Synthetic case | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 15 dB tone, key-down hops with no bar (of 208) | 51 | 40, still red |
| 10 dB tone (new test) | ΓÇô | 208 of 208, red |
| Loud noise alone, reads saying keying (of 1500) | 0 | 0 |
| Meter swing bar (`ConfidentSwingDb`) | 17 | 15 |

- **The tolerance formula as ruled changed nothing on its own.** Measured against the average of the gaps, the 15 dB tone reads about 16 dB, and the formula then gives 1.28 dB. That is under the 1.5 floor, so the result stayed at exactly 51.
- **What I did instead is my own decision, open to overrule.** I measured the contrast against the loudest noise hop in the gaps between paired bars. I also re-read a frequency bin's recent history once its contrast is first measured. With those, every element of the 15 dB tone after the first dah is an unbroken bar. The remaining 40 are the first dah (35 hops) plus 5 hops at the edges of the last two elements. Every variant I tried and took out is listed in the report, with its numbers.
- **Why the 10 dB tone still fails.** The instruction's estimate before a first gap exists is the bin's own lowest level, which sits about 20 dB under the noise. That makes a 10 dB tone look like about 30 dB of contrast, so it stays at the 1.5 floor and never makes a first pair. Using the bin's average level instead let noise read keying in 106 of 1500 reads, so I took it out.
- **Meter:** the 15.5 dB test profile was refused at 17 and accepted at 15; the same profile at 14.9 is still refused. Fifteen sits inside the 14.7 to 17.7 swing that empty test windows showed, so an empty band may now read as keying.
- **Record:** HM-DEC-187 is recorded, and 12.1 to 12.3 are re-ticked with test counts. Both builds were clean (0 warnings, 0 errors). The app carry-forward line was 278/278 at entry, after one re-run. At exit it was 277/278 after its one re-run. Every failure in both rounds was the known "dispatcher loop" error, counted neither way.

The report raises six items, none blocking:
1. What the contrast is measured against.
2. How a weak station makes its first pair.
3. The 15 dB test still at 40.
4. The risk of the meter reading keying on an empty band.
5. The wording of 12.1 and 12.2 no longer describes the code.
6. The two `PHASE_STATUS.md` copies differ.

When you tune the weaker stations again: a 15 dB station should show bars from its second element on, and a 10 dB one will probably still show nothing. Bars or a keying meter on an empty band are the thing to press *idiot* on.
